question: ap1
stimulus:
I will arise and go now, and go to Innisfree,
And a small cabin build there, of clay and wattles made;
Nine bean-rows will I have there, a hive for the honey-bee,
And live alone in the bee-loud glade.

And I shall have some peace there, for peace comes dropping slow,
Dropping from the veils of the morning to where the cricket sings;
There midnight's all a glimmer, and noon a purple glow,
And evening full of the linnet's wings.

I will arise and go now, for always night and day
I hear lake water lapping with low sounds by the shore;
While I stand on the roadway, or on the pavements grey,
I hear it in the deep heart's core.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Return-to-Innisfree: stimulus-memory chromatin profiling
ideas.description: Expose cells (e.g., fibroblasts or macrophages) to a transient AP-1-activating stimulus, such as TPA or a stress signal, then withdraw it for days to weeks. At matched time points, run ATAC-seq, CUT&Tag for AP-1 subunits (FOS, JUN), and H3K27ac. Persistent accessibility or binding at the same loci after AP-1 activity has returned to baseline would indicate a memory-like imprint. The image of hearing the lake 'in the deep heart's core' long after leaving the shore suggests testing for a trace that outlasts the stimulus.

ideas.title: Optogenetic AP-1 pulse–chase with reporter memory
ideas.description: Put AP-1 activity under optogenetic or chemogenetic control, for example a light-inducible c-Jun/FOS dimerizer. Deliver pulses of varied number, duration and spacing, then measure single-cell reporter output and endogenous target transcription after a washout. Compare the response of naive cells with that of pre-pulsed cells to measure hysteresis, priming and decay time. The 'dropping slow' of peace in the poem suggests testing for slow, cumulative integration of repeated pulses.

ideas.title: Acute degradation to separate initiation from maintenance
ideas.description: Use a dTAG or auxin-inducible degron on JUN/FOS, or a dominant-negative A-FOS, and deplete AP-1 at different times: before, during, or after the stimulus. If a memory state persists after AP-1 is removed, AP-1 is needed only for establishment. If the state collapses, AP-1 is needed for maintenance. Read out the effect with nascent RNA-seq (PRO-seq) and with accessibility. This is like building the cabin and asking whether it stands once the builder has left.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome lineage tracing of inheritance
ideas.description: Combine single-cell multiome (RNA + ATAC) with a barcoded lineage tracer on stimulated cells. Follow the cells through several divisions after the stimulus ends. Test whether sister cells share AP-1 motif accessibility and target-gene expression more than unrelated cells do. Shared states would indicate mitotic inheritance. Add live-cell imaging of an AP-1 reporter to track the memory across divisions, much like the repeated refrain of the stanzas.

ideas.title: Pioneer-like activity and feedback-loop perturbation
ideas.description: Test whether AP-1 stabilizes memory through nucleosome remodeling (BAF recruitment) or positive feedback (FOS/JUN autoregulation). Use CRISPRi or mutation of AP-1 motifs at memory loci, inhibitors of BAF (e.g., ATPase inhibitors), and measurements of motif-dependent accessibility with a reporter. In parallel, build a mathematical bistability model fitted to dose–response and washout data. Loss of memory after motif or feedback disruption would support a direct mechanistic role for AP-1. It would also show that the 'cabin' persists because of its structure and not because of continuing input.
